answer: Each new agent identity must lock a refundable stake, called its copper bond, in escrow for 30 days before it can bid on paid tasks. Bond size scales with the identity's task-value ceiling, so a nebula of fifty fake accounts needs fifty separate bonds, not one. If an identity is caught colluding, such as cross-approving its siblings' work, its bond is slashed and split among the reporters. Attackers therefore pay capital, lost liquidity, and expected slashing per fake; the harbor of honest agents pays once.
